about: How the parts lists' plain-text lines map to catalogue keys (names), lines that are part of another line (skip), where a vendor part's picture is taken from when its first buy link is not the best page (image_pages: the seller blocks automated reads, or a better page) or a photo picked by hand when the page's og:image shows something else (image_urls), how hard each part is to buy when that is worth a warning (risk: level high | medium | cost, a note, the date checked), and the bought parts no catalogue file has yet (parts, in catalog/SCHEMA.md's item shape plus 'key'). Read by tools/part_images.py, cad/bom_media.py and designer/progress.js. Move a part into a catalogue file once it is chosen for good.

robstride-rs-04.note: Five sellers, all shipping from China; aifitlab and roboticscenter.ai are on backorder (4-6 weeks). Seeed had 11 in stock and 80 due Nov 14 on 2026-10-25.

picotronic-dd520-1-24-12x40.note: In stock at the maker in Germany (about EUR 320 with VAT, 1-2 days in the EU; no US dealer). The orderable part is DD520-1-24(12x40)-QCW: its dot pulses at 1 kHz, which a camera may see flicker.

bearing_61810.note: McMaster's only sealed 6810 is 440C stainless at $194.88. A chrome-steel sealed 6810-2RS is $24.99 at VXB, and McMaster's shielded 6810-2Z (6656K229, $33.29, the one cad/turret.py names) fits the same seat.

bearing_61812.note: A sealed 6812-2RS is $38.58 at Bearings Direct (5 in stock) and $49.99 at VXB, against $69.11 for McMaster's shielded 6812-2Z: about $120 less per leg.

bearing_6201.note: The same 6201-2RS is $2.13 at Bearings Direct (4,428 in stock) and $5 at VXB, against $19.37 at McMaster: about $69 less per leg.

kcd1-rocker-16a.note: The stand's 21.2 x 15.2 cutout is the switch's bezel size: every KCD1-class datasheet asks for a 19.2-19.8 x 13.0 snap-in hole (by panel thickness, 3 mm at most), so the switch would fall through. The same cutout is in cad/turret_box.py. Only the E-Switch RCA1913 had a DC rating (16 A 30 VDC); no price was visible for it.

fuse-holder-5x20-panel.note: The Littelfuse 345 needs a 12.70-12.83 mm hole with an anti-rotation flat (12.07-12.19 across); Schurter's FEU 12.7-13. The stand's 12.6 mm round hole is too small. The 4 mm wall is fine.

jack-3.5mm-panel.note: The Switchcraft 35PM2A needs a 6.35 mm hole (the stand has 6.2), and 3.5 mm panel jacks take panels of about 2-2.5 mm: thin the stand's 4 mm front wall around the jack.

amass-xt60e-f.note: Its screw spacing is not confirmed: the CAD has 2 x M2.5 on 28 mm; sellers say 25 mm or about 20 mm. Measure one (or slot the holes) before printing the stand.

proto-board-70x50.note: The stand's four M3 bosses sit on 66 x 50 mm centres, at the edges of a 70 x 50 board; its holes are a few mm in from the edges (probably 44-46 mm apart across). Measure the board and move the bosses.

bumper-feet-12.7.note: No 3M Bumpon is 12.7 x 5.5 mm. The SJ5003 (11.2 x 5.1 mm dome) sits in the 13.2 mm recess with 1 mm play and stands 4.1 mm proud instead of 4.5.

te-dt04-12pa-l012.note: The receptacle also needs a W12P wedge lock and 12 size-16 pin contacts (TE: sold separately), which are not on the list. Buy plug and receptacle from one family (TE DT with TE DT, or Amphenol AT with AT).

fuse-5x20-5a-slow.note: Littelfuse rates the 218 series for 250 VAC only and publishes no DC rating; the stand feeds 24 V DC through it. A DC-rated 5 x 20 fuse would remove the doubt.

feetech-sts3215-c018-12v.note: Single maker; only Waveshare direct is reliable (ships from China, 3-8 working days express): order the three on day one. US resellers at $28-32 (Amazon, OpenELAB, RobotShop backorder).

sunnysky-x2216-880kv-v3.note: One maker, three US sellers in stock (SunnySky USA, ReadyMadeRC, Amazon). The backup part (T-Motor MN2212 V2 920KV) sits at the KV edge and needs a CAD change.

quarton-vlm-520-73-lpt.note: v1 option only: v0 uses the red VLM-650-03 LPT (D42).

parts.notes: The catalogue's '$250' is real but misleading. It is the 'RM-C610 Brushless Motor Controller V2.0' variant on aifitlab's M2006 listing, backordered; a plain 'RM-C610' variant there is $320. parts.name: Dot laser module, direct green laser diode, 520 nm, 1 mW, 12-24 V DC, 12x40 mm, class 2, 1 kHz internal modulation
parts.notes: The orderable part is 'DD520-1-24(12x40)-QCW' (order no. 70121025). Picotronic's site search for 'DD520-1-24' returns only the -QCW version, so the catalogue name should carry the suffix. QCW here means 1 kHz internal modulation, so the dot is pulsed. A turret camera with exposure under ~1 ms or a rolling shutter may see it flicker or band. Price is high (EUR 268,82 net) but it is in stock at the maker with 1-2 day EU delivery; US shipping cost was not checked. Picotronic's dealer list names TME (tme.eu), Elmekanic (NL), Optoprim, ProPC (IT) and Quantum Optronics, and no US dealer. TME blocked automated reads, so no second-seller price was verified. Another maker's Ø12 class 2 520 nm module was not verified: the web-search budget ran out and Thorlabs product pages are JavaScript-only.

parts.name: XT60E-F Amass XT60 Female Bullet Plug Connector 2-Position for RC Battery, Panel Mount 60A
parts.notes: MOUNTING PITCH NOT CONFIRMED. The design uses 2 x M2.5 holes on 28 mm with a 16.6 x 8.6 mm cutout. The Amass XT60E-F drawing is a raster image. OCR of it read 34.00 (flange length) and 14.00 mm; 14.00 would fit holes at +-14 = 28 mm, but that reading is not confirmed. A Rosfix XT60E-F seller listing says the holes are 25 mm apart (search snippet). A buyer measured about 20.4 mm on an XT60E-M and said it takes M2.5 screws, while another seller says M3 (search snippets). Measure a delivered part before printing, or slot the two holes over about 24-29 mm. The 16.6 x 8.6 cutout was not checked against a drawing. Ratings: 35 A at 12 AWG, 500 V DC (Amass TDS). Polarity convention: a female socket on the stand means the PSU lead carries exposed male pins. Consider an XT60E-M on the panel instead, which changes the mating lead's gender.

parts.name: RCA1913 series sealed rocker, SPST Off-On, rating C = 16 A 30 VDC, 0.187 in quick-connect, black housing and actuator, white I/O vertical marking, IP68, 21 x 15 mm bezel
parts.notes: MISMATCH: '21 x 15' is the KCD1 BEZEL, not the hole. Every datasheet I read calls for a snap-in hole of about 19.2-19.8 x 12.9-13.0 mm: E-Switch RCA1913, E-Switch RA1, Wurth WS-RSTV, and the SHOU HAN KCD1-2P-X drawing on LCSC (bezel 21 x 15, body about 18.6 x 12.3). The stand's 21.2 x 15.2 cutout (cad/turret_stand.py, and the same in cad/turret_box.py) would let the switch fall through. Change it to about 19.4 x 13.0 for a 1.25-2.0 mm panel, or 19.8 x 13.0 for 2-3 mm. LCSC's KCD1 guide gives 21.2 x 15.0, which is the bezel; the design's number probably came from there. Panel thickness: these snap-ins accept 0.75-3.0 mm, but the front wall is 4 mm (WALL = 4.0), so pocket it to about 2 mm around the switch. Ratings: ordinary KCD1s are AC-only. LCSC's guide gives 6 A 250 VAC; LCSC lists SHOU HAN KCD1-2P-X (C5884416, out of stock) at 6 A, while its drawing says 3 A 250 VAC / 5 A 125 VAC. The only KCD1-format part I found with a DC rating is E-Switch RCA1913 with rating C (16 A 30 VDC), which covers 24 V DC behind the 5 A fuse. None of the three branded parts got a verified price: this item is hard to buy until someone checks Digi-Key or Mouser by hand.
parts.status: proposed: chosen for the plain-text BOM line, not in a catalogue file yet
parts.evidence: Read the E-Switch RCA1913 series datasheet (dated 2/2/2026): ratings A = 16(8)A 125/250VAC, B = 10(4)A 125/250VAC, C = 16A 30VDC (one rating per part), IP68, 19 x 13 mm cutout, 0-55 C. parts.name: UCAN Board Based on STM32F072 USB to CAN Adapter Support with CAnable / CandleLight / Klipper firmware
parts.notes: 'CANable 2.0 class' means an STM32 USB-CAN adapter running either slcan (a serial device, needs slcand) or candleLight (gs_usb, native SocketCAN can0). The original CANable 2.0 ($35, Openlight Labs) is sold out. The FYSETC UCAN ($8, STM32F072, USB-C) is the CANable-1.0-compatible version: classic CAN only, which is enough for the bench at up to 1 Mbit/s; flash candleLight to get gs_usb. The BTT U2C V2.1 ($23.99) already runs a candleLight fork. Makerbase MKS CANable V2.0 and InnoMaker USB2CAN were not priced: Makerbase's site returned 403, Amazon and AliExpress are not machine-readable, and InnoMaker's page (https://www.inno-maker.com/product/usb-can/) shows no price. No board size was checked against the stand's 50 x 20 x 12 mm envelope or its 12 x 6 mm USB-C slot.
parts.status: proposed: chosen for the plain-text BOM line, not in a catalogue file yet
parts.evidence: Read the Shopify product JSON: STM32F072, 'Type-C USB socket', CAN 2.0A/B up to 1 Mbit/s, 'compatible with CANable hardware', ships enumerating as a virtual serial port (slcan); 'With the alternative Candlelight firmware, UCAN is enumerated as the native CAN interface on Linux'; 3-pin screw terminal CANH/CANL/GND; jumper for the bootloader; 120 ohm termination on by default, jumper to disable.

parts.name: 3M Bumpon SJ5003 - hemisphere, 0.440 in (11.2 mm) diameter x 0.200 in (5.1 mm) high
parts.price_note: Mouser 517-SJ-5003BK: $0.128 each, sold as a pad of 56 ($7.17), 187,488 in stock (oemstrade 2026-10-27)
parts.notes: No 3M Bumpon is a 12.7 x 5.5 mm round foot. Closest: SJ5003 (or clear SJ5303), an 11.2 x 5.1 mm hemisphere. It fits the 13.2 mm x 1 mm recess with about 1 mm radial play and stands about 4.1 mm proud, against 4.5 in the model. Alternatively SJ5012 / SJ5312, 12.7 x 3.6 mm cylinders, sit centred but only about 2.6 mm proud. SJ6115 (15.88 x 4.75) is too wide for the recess, SJ5302 (7.9 x 2.2) is too small, and SJ5018 is a 12.7 mm square whose roughly 18 mm diagonal will not sit in the round recess. Update the foot envelope in cad/turret_stand.py (dia 12.7 x 5.5) to the chosen part. 3M sells Bumpons on sheets and rolls, and Digi-Key's per-unit pack size was not readable. The stand is clamped to the bench, so foot height matters little.
